goal: RETIRE the graph/index.md catalog and its generator (engine issue #87; maintainer decision 2026-07-30: retire, not repair). The generator has been BROKEN since the RFC 0005 atomic-layout migration — index_regen._scan globs the pre-atomic graph/<section>/ path, so a live regen writes an EMPTY index (page_count 0) — and the file has been stale since 2026-06-13, six weeks unnoticed. It has zero code consumers (recall_v7 serves only `claim`; legacy recall serves only `learning_*`; no code path reads a wiki_index page — the generator is its only toucher), zero human consumers (the Obsidian workspace has never opened it), and Obsidian's native graph view / search / backlinks supersede a static 50KB catalog. ENGINE: delete runtime/service/jobs/index_regen.py; remove the `atelier_index_regen` MCP handler + its registration in runtime/service/tools.py; remove or adapt the index_regen assertions in tests/test_capability_ports.py; delete index_regen-only tests. KEEP the `wiki_index` page_type in schema/data/gorae.overlay.yaml (reasoning in _decision_wiki_index below). VAULT (exactly two files): delete graph/index.md, and edit graph/meta/dangling-baseline.yaml to prune the 35 `rfc-0005-index` entries (rewriting that category's disposition to record the retire) AND add the newly revealed target to `boundary-external`. DOCS: a CHANGELOG entry recording the retire, its evidence, the false-resolution finding, and that this is the fingerprint-waiver path's first real exercise.

waivers.reason: Deleting graph/index.md is the run's only fingerprinted change: file_digests walks *.md only, so the graph/meta/dangling-baseline.yaml edit contributes nothing to changed_paths. The fingerprint is a hash and cannot carry a numeric bound (§3.5), so it is released and the sibling count is bounded at exactly one path. Prefix scoping to `graph/` is NOT declared because the mechanism does not support it: vault_state.changed_paths returns a flat relpath list and contract.py accepts only {release, bound{metric,to}, reason} — no scope field exists. max:1 is the tightest bound this mechanism can express, and it is tighter than a prefix scope would be.

_arithmetic: 128 − 35 + 2 = 95, NOT 93. The 35 `rfc-0005-index` dangling edges are carried BY graph/index.md and leave entirely with it. The +2 are the two inbound edges the retire reveals: raw/personal/diary/2023/10/14.md and raw/personal/diary/2023/12/20.md both link [[_archive/projects/_archive/German Working Holiday/1-3.계획/index]]. Two edges, ONE new distinct target.
_false_resolution_finding: Those two links resolve to graph/index.md (page 6522) today ONLY because reindex._build_basename_index maps the basename `index` and 6522 is the vault's sole page with that basename. The resolution is SEMANTICALLY FALSE — an archived German-Working-Holiday folder index has nothing to do with the graph catalog. So the retire REMOVES A WRONG EDGE (a correctness improvement) and the two edges correctly become dangling: the content they name genuinely is not in this vault. Finding for the CHANGELOG: for a partial-key fallback, UNIQUENESS IS NOT RELEVANCE — a collision-safe basename index is safe against ambiguity but not against a unique-yet-unrelated match. Scale check already performed and not to be redone: 24 path-form wikilinks resolve to a page not matching their claimed path; 23 are LEGITIMATE migration-scar resolutions (wiki/entities/X → graph/atomic/X; G6's timestamp → claim). The `index` case is the only semantic mismatch, and it disappears with this retire.
_baseline_edit_must_add_as_well_as_prune: The revealed target `_archive/projects/_archive/German Working Holiday/1-3.계획/index` is NOT in graph/meta/dangling-baseline.yaml. A pure prune would push metrics.dangling_new.new 0 → 1 and break the RFC 0009 ratchet / doctor D8. metrics.dangling_new.new is default-denied at 0 by the envelope — no waiver — which is precisely why the baseline step must BOTH prune the 35 `rfc-0005-index` entries AND add the revealed target to `boundary-external` with a one-line note that it names content outside this vault and was masked until the retire by a basename false-resolution. The `_`-prefixed diagnostics (_accepted, _current_distinct: 87 → 53) do move, but they are outside the numeric namespace (§5.1.1) and are unwaivable by construction.
_decision_wiki_index: KEEP the `wiki_index` page_type in schema/data/gorae.overlay.yaml. Disclosed reasoning: (a) an adopter's legacy vault may still hold wiki/index.md, and dropping the classification would make such a file classify as unknown or trip lint; (b) tests/test_regression_gorae_vault.py already asserts wiki/index.md → wiki_index, so removal is not a no-op even inside this repo; (c) the page_type is a classification rule in schema data, decoupled from the generator being deleted — retiring a producer does not require retiring the type it produced. The conservative choice costs one inert overlay entry; the aggressive one risks breaking a vault this contract has no measurement over.
_envelope_reasoning: Default-deny over the §3.4 namespace with exactly one waiver. Explicitly expected UNCHANGED and left default-denied: metrics.dangling_new.new (0), metrics.cross_project_noise.* (measured from the pinned out-of-tree fixture), census.* (the census counts only claim/entity/source, so wiki_index is not a census kind and INV-1 is unaffected by deleting the page), guard_liveness, pending_age, promote_eligible, lens_param_present, surfacing.*, eval.*.
_pins_reasoning: before_sha256 c08118cd… is the sha256 of ~/.atelier/cache/goals/G7-index-regen-retire/before.json, whose metrics.dangling_links reads by_type.wikilink 128 / total 128 — the FRESH round baseline both INTENT clauses bind from. captured_at_head bbc194e2… is the current main HEAD and becomes this contract commit's first parent (§3.1.1). fixture_sha256 458a262e… is pinned because metrics.cross_project_noise.* lives in this run's ENVELOPE namespace and is measured from ~/.atelier/fixtures/project_probes.json; --fixture feeds only the pin check and the metric is measured from the default fixture either way, so an unpinned enveloped leaf could be moved by a mid-run fixture edit with nothing to catch it. fixture_path is a TOP-LEVEL field BESIDE the pins block, not inside it: freeze.check_pins raises when pins.fixture_sha256 is set and no top-level fixture_path is declared (prose in a note does not count). Two prior runs aborted on exactly this — G1 r1 pinned a fixture that did not exist; G7 r2 pinned a real one but wrote its path only in prose.
_supersedes_reasoning: Empty. INV-4 surfacing.visible must not fall and eval recall must not regress — no recall path serves a wiki_index page (recall_v7 serves only `claim`, legacy recall only `learning_*`), so neither moves and there is nothing to release. INV-1 is untouched: the census counts only claim/entity/source, and graph/index.md is none of those. The embedding provider is healthy and eval._engine_label() reads `hybrid`, so the §4.2 engine gate holds.
_out_of_scope: Do NOT touch any other vault file; do NOT edit the two diary bodies (their links are honestly broken — that is the true state this retire reveals); do NOT alter other dangling-baseline categories; do NOT 'fix' the remaining accepted dangling residual.

Verified INDEPENDENTLY against the live projection, not by re-reading the author summary: broken wikilink edges total 128 (matches pins/before.json); links FROM graph/index.md (page 7312) with to_page_id IS NULL = 35; links INTO graph/index.md = exactly 2, both from raw/personal/diary/2023/{10/14,12/20}.md targeting the same archived German-Working-Holiday path. graph/index.md is the vault SOLE page with basename index.md, so both inbound edges necessarily break on deletion. 128 - 35 + 2 = 95 is exact, and eq (not max) is therefore the correct form.

A prune-only baseline edit reaches 95 on both INTENT clauses but pushes metrics.dangling_new.new from 0 to 1 (accepted 87-35=52 vs current distinct 87-35+1=53), and that metric is default-denied at 0 with no waiver. ENVELOPE: default-deny with exactly one waiver. vault.content_fingerprint is a hash and cannot carry a numeric bound, so the release/bound split onto vault.changed_paths.count {max:1} is the canonical §3.5 pattern (contract.py:233-259). max:1 is exact, not slack: before.json _file_digests holds 7304 entries and ZERO .yaml paths, so the dangling-baseline.yaml edit contributes nothing to changed_paths and graph/index.md is the single changed path. Verified the disclosed limitation is real: vault_state.changed_paths returns a flat relpath list and the waiver schema accepts only {release, bound, reason} with no scope field, so a graph/ prefix scope is genuinely inexpressible and max:1 is strictly tighter.

critic.noted_not_blocking: No metric in the §3.4 namespace measures the engine tool surface, so the ENGINE half of the goal (delete index_regen.py, drop the atelier_index_regen handler and registration, adapt/delete its tests) carries no expressible bound.
